title: Steady Drift: release canvas, calendar & notes (mar 2026)
content:
Purpose and context:
This is a lightweight, operational canvas for the March 2026 steady-drift release. Goal is low-friction rollout of feature set B (latency-tier routing + batching tweak) with minimal customer-visible impact. Use as the single source for the on-call shift, release shepherd, and product PM during the 48h ramp window.

High-level objectives:
- Deploy feature B behind feature-flag with progressive traffic introduction.
- Maintain p95 < 350ms for hosted API; keep error rate delta < 0.1% vs baseline.
- Validate cost signal (tokens/sec per GPU) doesn't exceed baseline +12%.
- Capture canary metrics and a short postdeploy regression check within 4h.

Assumptions / risks (things to watch):
- Autoscaler may overshoot during traffic bursts (see note about throttle knob below).
- New batching path interacts poorly with short-sequence workloads (spike in tail latency).
- SLO targets are tight during APAC morning; prefer to schedule quiet-window where possible.

Coasting plan (calendar):
- T-72h (2026-03-03): final smoke artifact build, integration tests, release notes draft put into customer-facing doc.
- T-48h (2026-03-05): cut release candidate, internal staging rollout to 5% infra (no customer traffic). Quick perf sweep (10k reqs) against synthetic traffic.
- T-24h (2026-03-06): narrow canary to 1% production traffic for 1h, then 5% for 2h if signals green.
- T+0 (2026-03-07 09:00 PT): begin progressive ramp: 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 6h windows.
- T+6h: stabilization buffer (monitoring + manual signoff).
- T+24h: evaluate rollback gates; if green, continue to full rollout.
- T+48h: postmortem notes + retro starter appended; mark release stable.

Short checklist (for release shepherd):
- Preflight:
  - Verify RC image checksum and diff against last good (build id saved).
  - Confirm observability dashboards live (latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, token throughput).
  - Confirm alerting thresholds (temporary canary thresholds set).
  - Patch release notes: short TL;DR, breaking changes, opt-out instructions, expected behavior changes.
  - Slack channel created: #release-steady-drift (invite on-call, SRE, PM, eng lead).

- Canary rollout knobs:
  - Traffic ramp schedule (as above) and an explicit throttle (manual abort button) in the console.
  - Autoscaler soft-limit reduced by 10% for first 6h to prevent overshoot.
  - Enable prefix/KV cache snapshotting for reuse in case of rollback.

- Night-of actions (operator):
  - T-30m: run short smoke tests against canary endpoint (auth, basic prompt round-trip).
  - T+1h after each ramp step: verify telemetry (latency, errors, GPU utilization).
  - If any alert fires: immediately pause ramp and run rollback test harness.

Rollback matrix (quick decision rules):
- Critical (automatic): 5xx rate > 0.5% sustained for 5 minutes or p95 > 600ms for 5 minutes -> initiate rollback.
- High (manual): p95 delta > +200ms vs baseline for 30 minutes -> hold ramp and escalate.
- Cost (manual): tokens/sec per GPU > baseline +20% across ≥2 clusters -> hold ramp and investigate.

Monitoring & signals to prioritize:
- Synthetics: real-world prompts from sample set (short/long distributions).
- Production metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx/4xx error rates, request rate, token throughput per GPU, KV cache hit rate.
- Infra: pod restarts, OOM, autoscaler scaling events.
- Business: API quota spikes, payment/fraud anomalies (FYI to ops).

Release notes (customer-facing draft - short):
Title: Steady Drift release — March 2026
Overview: Small improvements to request routing and batching that reduce median latency for long-context calls and lower tail-cost for mid-size requests.
What’s new:
- Smarter route selection: requests under 512 tokens favor low-latency fast-path by default (no customer action).
- Batching tuning: background batching is more aggressive for midsize workloads; expected to reduce cost by ~6% for common workloads.
- Console: new manual throttle control for progressive rollouts.
Notes and impacts:
- No breaking changes to the API.
- Edge case: extremely short calls (<20 tokens) may see slight tail latency increase; we have a toggle to opt-out per-tenant if needed.
- We will monitor and roll back if customer-facing errors increase.

Known issues (internal):
- Occasionally higher p99 on short-seq traffic during high concurrency in us-west-2. Root cause investigation ticket: ENGREL-328.
- Minor mismatch in billing sampling for deduped batching slice (investigating).

Communications plan:
- Internal: 09:00 PT release brief posted to #release-steady-drift. Ops shift to post hourly updates during ramp.
- Customers: email to beta group at T+6h if green; broader announcement after full rollout.
- Support doc updated with opt-out instructions and rollback contact.

Post-release checklist (T+24h and T+48h):
- Collect perf snapshots vs baseline and attach to this doc.
- Mark follow-up tickets for any telemetry anomalies.
- Short retro: what went well, what tripped us, immediate action items (assign owners).

Notes to self / open questions:
- Should we warm the new batching kernel in staging longer to avoid the us-west blip? (action: Jin to run extended soak 24h).
- Can we add a lightweight canary signal for cache-hit-rate delta to the dashboard? (Lena to prototype).
- Do we want a temporary rate-limit soft-cushion for free-tier customers during ramp? (PM call needed).

Appendix: quick command snippets (for shift)
- Pause ramp: /release pause steady-drift
- Force rollback: /release rollback steady-drift --target last-known-good
- Collect smoke logs: /infra collect-logs --since 15m --tag steady-drift

End notes: Keep this doc as the ephemeral operational canvas — post-mortem will consolidate final artifacts and a cleaned release note. If you add anything here, prefix with initials and timestamp.

-- AP (Aisha) 2026-03-14: initial draft and orchard of checks; will iterate after staging run.
